questions.q: Let the curve $z(1+i)+\bar{z}(1-i)=4, z \in \mathrm{C}$, divide the region $|z-3| \leq 1$ into two parts of areas $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then $|\alpha-\beta|$ equals :

questions.q: If $z$ and $\omega$ are two complex numbers such that \left|z\omega\right| = 1$ and $arg\left(z\right) - arg( \omega ) = \dfrac{π}{2}$, then:$

questions.solution:
Let \left|z\right| = r$ and $arg\left(z\right) = \theta,$~given~$arg\left(z\right) - arg\left(\omega\right) = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$⇒ \theta - arg\left(\omega\right) = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$⇒ arg\left(\omega\right) = \theta - \dfrac{π}{2}$

We know that, if~\left|z\right| = r \text{ and } arg\left(z\right) = \theta$~then~$1\left|z\right| = \dfrac{1}{r} \text{ and } arg\left(\overset{¯}{z}\right) = - arg\left(z\right) = - \theta,$

Hence,~\left|\omega\right| = \dfrac{1}{r}$ and~$arg( \overset{¯}{ω} ) = - arg\left(\omega\right) = \dfrac{π}{2} - \theta$

Now, by using Euler form i.e. if~\left|z\right| = r \text{ and } arg\left(z\right) = \theta,$~then~$z = re^{i\theta},$~we have~$z = re^{i\theta}$ and $\omega = \dfrac{1}{r}e^{i ( \theta - \dfrac{\pi}{2} )}$

Also,~$\overset{¯}{z}\omega = re^{- i\theta} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{r}e^{i \left(\theta - $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{z}\omega =$e^{- i\dfrac{π}{2}}$

Using polar form i.e. e^{i\theta} =cos\theta ++isin\theta,$~we get

$\overset{¯}{z}\omega =$1\l$left[cos\left(- $\dfrac{π}{2}\right) +$isin\left(- $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)\right] = -i$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{z}\omega = -$i .$

$

questions.q: Let ${z}_{1} = 2 + 3i$ and ${z}_{2} = 3 + 4i$. The set~$S = \left\{z \in C: \left|z - {z}_{1}\right|2 - \left|z - {z}_{2}\right|2 = \left|{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|2\right\}$& represents a
options: straight line with sum of its intercepts on the coordinate axes equals $14$
hyperbola with the length of the transverse axis $7$
straight line with the sum of its intercepts on the coordinate axes equals $- 18$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

${z}_{1} = 2 + 3i$ and ${z}_{2} = 3 + 4i$~and the set

$S = \left\{z \in C: \left|z - {z}_{1}\right|2 - \left|z - {z}_{2}\right|2 = \left|{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|2\right\}$,

Now putting the value of~$z = x + iy, {z}_{1} = 2 + 3i$~and~${z}_{2} = 3 + 4i$~in~\left|z - {z}_{1}\right|2 - \left|z - {z}_{2}\right|2 = \left|{z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right|2$~we get,

$⇒ \left(( x - 2{)}^{2} + ( y - 3{)}^{2}\right) - \left(( x - 3{)}^{2} - ( y - 4{)}^{2}\right) = 1 + 1$

$⇒ x + y = 7$

Which is a straight line with intercept~$7$~on~$x \text{ and } y$~axis, so sum of intercept will be~$7 + 7 = 14$.

$

questions.q: Let $n$~denote the number of solutions of the equation $z^{2} + 3\overset{¯}{z} = 0,$~where $z$ is a complex number. Then the value of $\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{∞}\dfrac{1}{nk}$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $z^{2} + 3\overset{¯}{z} = 0$

Put~$z = x + iy,$~then we know that~$\overset{¯}{z} = x - iy,$~hence, we have

\left(x + iy\right)2 + 3\left(x - iy\right) = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + i^{2}y^{2} + 2ixy + 3x - 3iy = 0$

We also, know that~$i^{2} = - 1,$~hence, we get

$⇒ x^{2} - y^{2} + 2ixy + 3x - 3iy = 0$

$⇒ \left(x^{2} - y^{2} + 3x\right) + i ( 2xy - 3y ) = 0 + i0$

On comparing the real and imaginary parts, we get

$x^{2} - y^{2} + 3x = 0 \ldots \left(1\right)$

And~$2xy - 3y = 0 \ldots \left(2\right)$

$⇒ y\left(2x - 3\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{3}{2},y = 0$

Put $x = \dfrac{3}{2}$in equation~\left(1\right),$~we get~$\dfrac{9}{4} -y^{2} + \dfrac{9}{2} =0$

$⇒ y^{2} = \dfrac{27}{4}$

$⇒ y = \pm \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} .$

$⇒ \left(x, y\right) = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\right), \left(\dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{- 3\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) .$

Now, put~$y = 0,$~in the equation~\left(1\right),$~we get~$x^{2} + 3x = 0$

$⇒ x = 0, - 3 .$

$∴ \left(x, y\right) = \left(0, 0\right), \left(-3, 0\right) .$

$∴$ No of solutions$= n = 4$

Now,~$\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{∞} \left(\dfrac{1}{nk}\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{∞}\left(\dfrac{1}{4k}\right)

$= $\dfrac{1}{1} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{16} + \dfrac{1}{64} + \ldots \ldots

The above progression is a geometric progression, with first term~$a = 1$~and common ratio~$r = $\dfrac{1}{4}~and the sum of infinite terms of the geometric progression is~\dfrac{a}{1 - r}

Thus,~$\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{∞} \left(\dfrac{1}{nk}\right) =$1 \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{4}\right)$

$= 1\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) = \dfrac{4}{3} .$

$

questions.solution:
The work done in stopping the car and the truck can be written as

$\begin{cases}W & = & Fx \\ & = & ∆ KE\end{cases}$

As both the car and the truck are moving initially with the same kinetic energy, after being stopped, they will have the same change of kinetic energy.

Also, they are stopped with the same applied force.

Hence, from the above equation, it can be written that~they have the same displacement, i.e.,~${x}_{1} = {x}_{2}$.

Acceleration is a vector quantity. As the direction of motion of the car is different in the two given situations, the acceleration of the car will not be the same.

questions.subject: Mathematics

$

Now putting the value of~$z = x + iy$~in~$\dfrac{2z - 3i}{2z + i}$~we get,

$\dfrac{2\left(x + iy\right) - 3i}{2 \left($x + iy\right) + i} = \left($2x + $i \left($2y - 3\right)\right)\left(2x + i \left($2y + 1\right)\$right)\left(2x - i \left(2y + 1\right)\right)\left(2x - i\left(2y + 1\right)\right)$

Now taking real part as,

$⇒ 4x^{2} + 4y^{2} - 4y - 3 = 0$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} - y - $\dfrac{3}{4} =$0$

Now using,

$x + y^{2} = 0⇒ x = - y^{2}$~we get,

$⇒ y^{4} + y^{2} - y - $\dfrac{3}{4} =$0$

$⇒ y^{4} + y^{2} - y = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{z \in \mathbb{C}: z^{2} + \overset{¯}{z} = 0\right\}$. Then $\mathop{∑}_{z \in S} \left(Re  \left($z\right) + Im \left($z\right)\right)& is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$S = \left\{z \in C: z^{2} + \overset{¯}{z} = 0\right\}$

Let~$z = x + iy$

$z^{2} = x^{2} - y^{2} + 2ixy$

$\overset{¯}{z} = x - iy$

Now putting the value~in~$z^{2} + \overset{¯}{z}$~we get,

$z^{2} + \overset{¯}{z} = x^{2} - y^{2} + x + i\left(2xy - y\right) = 0$

Now on comparing both side we get,

$⇒ x^{2} + x - y^{2} = 0$~and~$2xy - y = 0$

$⇒ y = 0$~or~$x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now if~$y = 0; x = 0, - 1$

If~$x = \dfrac{1}{2}\text{then}y = \dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{- \sqrt{3}}{2}$

So,~$\mathop{∑}_{z \in S}\left(Re \left(z\right) + Im \left(z\right) = \left(0 - 1 + \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 0 + 0 + \dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{3}{2}\right) = 0$

questions.q: If $\alpha$ is a root of the equation $x^2+x+1=0$ and $\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\left(\alpha^{\mathrm{k}}+\frac{1}{\alpha^{\mathrm{k}}}\right)^2=20$, then n is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \alpha=\omega \\ & \therefore\left(\omega^k+\frac{1}{\omega^k}\right)^2=\omega^{2 k}+\frac{1}{\omega^{2 k}}+2 \\ & =\omega^{2 k}+\omega^k+2 \quad \because \omega^{3 k}=1\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}}\left(\omega^{2 \mathrm{k}}+\omega^{\mathrm{k}}+2\right)=20 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\omega^2+\omega^4+\omega^6+\ldots+\omega^{2 \mathrm{n}}\right)+\left(\omega+\omega^2+\omega^3+\ldots+\right. \\ & \left.\omega^{\mathrm{n}}\right)+2 \mathrm{n}=20
\end{aligned}$
Now if $n=3 m, \quad m \in I$
Then $0+0+2 \mathrm{n}=20 \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=10$ (not satisfy)
if $n=3 m+1$, then
$\begin{aligned}
& \omega^2+\omega+2 \mathrm{n}=20 \\ & -1+2 \mathrm{n}=20 \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=\frac{21}{2}(\text { not possible })
\end{aligned}$
if $n=3 m+2$,
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(\omega^8+\omega^{10}\right)+\left(\omega^4+\omega^5\right)+2 \mathrm{n}=20 \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\omega^2+\omega\right)+\left(\omega+\omega^2\right)+2 \mathrm{n}=20 \\ & 2 \mathrm{n}=22 \\ & \mathrm{n}=11 \text { satisfy } \mathrm{n}=3 \mathrm{~m}+2 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{n}=11
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let the complex numbers $\alpha$ and $1\overset{¯}{α}$ lie on the circles \left|z - {z}_{0}\right|2 = 4$ and \left|z - {z}_{0}\right|2 = 16$ respectively, where ${z}_{0} = 1 + i$. Then, the value of $100 | \alpha{|}^{2}$ is__________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: \left|z - {z}_{0}\right|2 = 4$

$⇒ \left(z - {z}_{0}\right)\left(z - {z}_{0}\right) = 4$

$⇒ z z - {z}_{0}z - {z}_{0} z + \left|{z}_{0}\right|2 = 4$

$⇒ \left|z\right|2 - {z}_{0}z - {z}_{0} z = 2\left\{\text{as}\left|{z}_{0}\right|2 = 2\right\}$

It is given that, $\alpha$ lies on \left|z - {z}_{0}\right|2 = 4$.

$⇒ \left|\alpha\right|2 - \alpha{z}_{0} - {z}_{0} \alpha -2 = 0 . . . \left(i\right)$

We know that, $\alpha \cdot \alpha = \left|\alpha\right|2 = \left|\alpha\right|2$

\left|z - {z}_{0}\right|2 = 16$

$⇒ \left(1\overset{¯}{α} - {z}_{0}\$right)\left(\dfrac{1}{α} - \overset{¯}{z}$0\right) = 16$

$⇒ \left($1 - \overset{¯}{α}{z}_{0}\right)\left(1 - \alpha\overset{¯}{z}0\right) = 16 | \alpha{|}^{2}$

$⇒ 1 - \overset{¯}{α}{z}_{0} - \alpha\overset{¯}{z}0 + | \alpha{|}^{2}\left|{z}_{0}\right|2 = 16 | \alpha{|}^{2}$

$⇒ 1 - \overset{¯}{α}{z}_{0} - \alpha\overset{¯}{z}0 = 14 | \alpha{|}^{2} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Using, \left(i\right)\text{and} \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ 5 | \alpha{|}^{2} =1$

$⇒ 100 | \alpha{|}^{2} =20$

$

questions.q: Let $z$ and $w$ be two complex numbers such that~$w = z\overset{¯}{z} - 2z + 2,  \left|$\dfrac{z + i}{z - 3i}\right| =$1$ and $Re \left(w\right)$~has minimum value. Then, the minimum value of $n \in N$ for which $w^{n} is real, is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\omega = z\overset{¯}{z} - 2z + 2$

\left|\dfrac{z + i}{z - 3i}\right| = 1$

$⇒ \left|z + i\right| = \left|z - 3i\right|$

$⇒ x^{2} + \left(y + 1\right)2 = x^{2} + \left(y - 3\right)2$

$⇒ y = 1$

$⇒ z = x + i, x \in R$

$\omega = \left(x + i\right)\left(x - i\right) - 2\left(x + i\right) + 2$

$= x^{2} + 1 - 2x - 2i + 2$

$Re \left(\omega\right) = x^{2} - 2x + 3 = \left(x - 1\right)2 + 2$

For min~\left(Re\left(\omega\right)\right), x = 1$

$⇒ \omega = 2 - 2i = 2\left(1 - i\right) = 2\sqrt{2}e^{- i\dfrac{π}{4}}$

${ω}^{n} = \left(2\sqrt{2}\right)ne^{- i\dfrac{n\pi}{4}}$

For real and minimum value of $n$,

$n = 4$
